To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the risk of cancer induction in the conceptus due to a diagnostic exposure is low (around 1/10 000/mGy) and that the risk is higher in the first trimester than in the third trimester (due to the higher radiosensitivity of the embryo and the higher absorbed dose in the embryo).
the risk of cancerogenesis due to in uteropregnant exposure to diagnostic X rays in a pregnant patient is extremely small and that the risk of tissue reaction is negligible.

the risk of stochastic effects of radiation exposure during pregnancy is low, that the risk is higher during the first trimester, that there is a threshold dose of 100mGY for tissue reactions, and that there is no evidence that the risk of cancer is higher in children of mothers who had an X ray examination during their pregnancy.
